title: Signed integral pullback Roos shift coordinates and derived descent
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, schemes $X,Y$ in the same universe as $E$, and a morphism $g:X\to Y$. Use the tower transition endomorphism of [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Use the completed coefficient module categories, strict finite-reduction pullback tower $B_g(P)$, Roos cochain functor $F_g(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_{B_g(P)})[-1]$, good (flat-term K-flat) representatives, derived pullback $D_g$, and retained representative comparison $\varepsilon_P:D_g(QP)\simeq QF_g(P)$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Here $Q$ is complex localization, and the natural-number index $n$ represents positive quotient exponent $n+1$.
Define $\operatorname{levelShift}_{P,r,n}:B_g(P[r])_n\simeq B_g(P)_n[r]$ by the canonical cochain shift of the additive finite module pullback composite. Define $\operatorname{productShift}_{P,r}:\prod_nB_g(P[r])_n\simeq(\prod_nB_g(P)_n)[r]$ by the product of these maps followed by the inverse product-preservation comparison of shift. Define $\operatorname{roosEnd}_P=1-s_{B_g(P)}$, with its actual quotient transitions.
For a shift-commutation structure $c$ on $F_g$, define $\operatorname{ShiftCoordinates}(c)$ to mean that for every complex $P$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$, its component $c_{r,P}:F_g(P[r])\to F_g(P)[r]$ is unsigned on the unshifted product summand and multiplied by $(-1)^r$ on the product summand shifted by $-1$, via $\operatorname{productShift}_{P,r}$ and the standard cochain degree reindexing. Thus in mapping-cocone coordinates it is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^r y)$, equivalently in reversed coordinates $(y,x)\mapsto((-1)^r y,x)$. The predicate is the two component equations, for every degree and every adjacent pair of degrees.
For such $c$ and a shift-commutation structure $d$ on $D_g$, define $\operatorname{ShiftDescent}(c,d)$ to mean: for every good $P$ and integer $r$, $P[r]$ is good and
$$\varepsilon_P[r]\circ d_{r,QP}=\eta_{F_g(P)}\circ Q(c_{r,P})\circ\varepsilon_{P[r]}\circ D_g(\eta_P^{-1}),$$
where $\eta_P:Q(P[r])\simeq(QP)[r]$ is the standard localization shift comparison. Both predicates only specify normalization; they assert neither the existence of $c,d$ nor the integral/completed pullback comparison.
